title: Sheet
description: A bare rounded screen with the front of a record sleeve on it, the cover and then title, artist, year and side one set label against value on the same axis as the credits, and a bottom sheet of song credits set like the back of a sleeve: labels flush right against an axis at a quiet weight, values flush left from it on one 24pt line pitch, the personnel set name against parts on that same axis, titles that hang, and side two's running times totted up in tabular figures. Drag the sheet and it stays exactly under your finger; let go and the speed you let go at is projected forward to choose peek, half or full, then a spring carries that speed in, and you can catch it mid-flight. Past full it rubber-bands. Half stops just under the year, so the sheet's side two carries on the page's side one. As it rises from half to full the record page behind steps back the way iOS does it: it scales to 0.94, its corners round, it dims a little, and the clock flips to light as a whole once the page's edge passes it, all in step with your finger, so dragging down from full brings the page forward continuously. At full the credits scroll, and a drag that scrolls them back to the top keeps going and pulls the sheet down in the same gesture. A click on the header steps up, Escape and the arrow keys step through the detents.
intent: The motion is Emil Kowalski's Vaul drawer and iOS sheets with detents: the drag follows the pointer one to one, release velocity picks the detent, damping past the edge instead of a hard stop, the presenting page scaling back with rounded corners, and scroll handing off to the drag only at the top. The phone is reduced to its glass so none of that has to compete with a mock of iOS; what the sheet carries instead is a 1969 credit block, typeset on a centred axis the way record sleeves and film titles set name against role.
